answer: Each epoch, every agent authorizes a $1 micro-charge on a payment card; only a tokenized fingerprint is stored, never the number. The registry rejects any fingerprint already tied to another identity, and a reused card freezes both accounts and burns their stake. The charge must clear a real processor, so virtual-card farms trip fraud blocks before scaling. A new card costs about $3, so 100 fakes cost $300 in cards plus $100 in charges each epoch. Like a cedar, trust grows one ring at a time; in this meadow no two agents share one root. A vault with one key per agent admits no crowd.
